samples.summary: `normalizeRowHeights` (plural) is exported but has zero consumers anywhere in the repo, and is not re-exported from either package entry
samples.evidence: `packages/docs/src/model/row-height.ts:42` defines and exports `normalizeRowHeights`. A repo-wide grep for `normalizeRowHeights` returns only that definition — no import, no test, and neither `packages/docs/src/index.ts:95` nor `packages/docs/src/node.ts:135` re-exports it (both list only `MAX_ROW_HEIGHT, normalizeRowHeight`). knip's docs workspace entry is `src/index.ts` only, so an unused export in a non-entry source file is exactly what it reports. Either wire it up (the natural caller is the `rowHeights` map in `crdt-tree.ts:216`, which currently maps `normalizeRowHeight` by hand) or drop it.

samples.summary: `MAX_FONT_SIZE` silently duplicates the frontend's `FONT_SIZE_MAX`; raising the picker's ceiling would make the docs reader drop sizes the picker can produce
samples.evidence: `packages/frontend/src/components/text-formatting/font-catalog.ts:74` declares `export const FONT_SIZE_MAX = 400;` and `clampFontSize` (line 83) is what the size picker commits. `packages/docs/src/model/numeric-attrs.ts:44` independently declares `MAX_FONT_SIZE = 400` and its doc comment asserts the two are the same number. They are today, but nothing enforces it: bump `FONT_SIZE_MAX` to 500 and `normalizeFontSize` starts returning `undefined` for a size the picker just wrote, which reads as "inherit" — the font size vanishes for every reader including the author after a refresh. The frontend has no `tsc` and no lane compares the two, so this drifts silently. Import the docs constant into `font-catalog.ts` (or vice-versa) rather than restating it.

samples.summary: The paste sanitizer bypasses four of the five new bands — it clamps `listLevel` but admits any finite `fontSize`, `lineHeight`, cell `padding`, `rowHeights` and image size
samples.evidence: `packages/docs/src/view/clipboard.ts` now imports `MAX_LIST_LEVEL` and clamps `listLevel` at line 351, but every sibling numeric passes through bare `asNumber` (line 69-71: finite-only, no ceiling): `fontSize` at lines 141/211, `lineHeight` at line 184, cell `padding` at line 234, `rowHeights` at line 298, and image `width`/`height` at lines 113-116. `table-layout.ts:246` explicitly acknowledges this for `rowHeights` ("the paste path (`sanitizeTableData`) admits any finite number") but the other four got no equivalent treatment. Consequence beyond geometry: a pasted image wider than `MAX_IMAGE_SIZE` (20000) is written to the CRDT and then dropped by `isPaintableImageSize` on every read — the picture disappears for the author too once the store re-reads, with its `src` still stored. The new bands are cheap to apply here; `clipboard.ts` already imports from `model/list-level.js`.

samples.summary: `Doc.setRowHeight` writes `tableData.rowHeights` with no band, so the one local write boundary is the only path that can still store an out-of-band height
samples.evidence: `packages/docs/src/model/document.ts:1183` does `td.rowHeights[rowIndex] = height;` with no `normalizeRowHeight`. Both *read* boundaries were banded by this change (`crdt-tree.ts:216`, `yorkie-doc-store.ts:470`) and `table-layout.ts:253` bands at layout, so a height written here above `MAX_ROW_HEIGHT` is stored and broadcast but honoured by nobody — the row silently snaps back to 10000px on the next read for the author and for every peer. The drag path (`text-editor.ts:2227`, `table-resize.ts:60`) reads the already-clamped `LayoutTable.rowHeights`, so this is hard to reach by dragging; a programmatic caller or a future host is what it costs. Banding at the write keeps the stored value and the rendered one in agreement.
searchedFor: grep table-resize.ts / text-editor.ts row drag height computation

samples.summary: `paginatableRowHeight` clamps the row height the paginator consumes, but the other consumers of the same `LayoutTable.rowHeights` array are unchanged, so painted and hit-test geometry disagree with pagination for a row past the bound
samples.evidence: `packages/docs/src/view/pagination.ts:132` now paginates `paginatableRowHeight(tl.rowHeights[ri], contentHeight)` while every sibling reader still uses the raw entry: hit-testing at `packages/docs/src/view/text-editor.ts:5522` (`relY < layoutTable.rowYOffsets[r] + layoutTable.rowHeights[r]`), selection rects at `packages/docs/src/view/selection.ts:617` and `:641`, cell painting at `packages/docs/src/view/table-renderer.ts:171`/`:201`, merged-cell geometry at `packages/docs/src/view/table-geometry.ts:169`, and resize handles at `packages/docs/src/view/table-resize.ts:60`. `tl.rowYOffsets` and `tl.totalHeight` are likewise unclamped. For a content-derived row taller than `MAX_ROW_PAGE_SPAN` pages the paginator stops emitting pages while the renderer still believes the row extends further, so carets, selection rectangles and row borders land on the wrong page. Only reachable with absurd (poisoned) content heights — which is precisely the case the clamp exists for — so the defence is incomplete rather than wrong. Clamping inside `computeTableLayout` (where step 5b already normalizes) would give every consumer the same number.

samples.summary: Slides keeps its own copy of the list-level ceiling and its pptx import writes `listLevel` unbanded, so `MAX_LIST_LEVEL` is not the single definition the new module claims to be
samples.evidence: `packages/slides/src/export/pptx/text.ts:85` hardcodes `Math.min(8, n)` and `packages/slides/src/import/pptx/text.ts:268` does `block.listLevel = list.level;` with no clamp at all. Slides text boxes hold docs `Block`s (see the `listLevel` in the API surface at `packages/slides/src/view/editor/text-box-editor.ts:263`) but they live in the slides CRDT and never pass through `crdt-tree.ts` or `yorkie-doc-store.ts`, so none of the new read-boundary bands apply to them. `packages/docs/src/model/list-level.ts:7` states the ceiling is defined once; in practice slides restates it, and a change to `MAX_LIST_LEVEL` would leave the pptx exporter emitting a different `lvl` than the editor allows. Importing `MAX_LIST_LEVEL`/`normalizeListLevel` from `@wafflebase/docs` in these two files removes the copy.

samples.summary: The cursor-only branch of the docs walker now does a sibling lookup on every invocation, including the toolbar block-style path that has no use for it
samples.evidence: `packages/docs/src/view/editor.ts:1724` calls `siblingsOf(block)` unconditionally, and `Doc.siblingBlocksOf` (`packages/docs/src/model/document.ts:311-327`) linearly scans the body, header and footer top-level arrays and can fall back to a full recursive walk of every table when the parent map misses. That work happens for `applyBlockStyle` at `packages/docs/src/view/editor.ts:3419` and the other `forEachBlockInSelection` callers, none of which read the second parameter. Not hot enough to matter (these are toolbar gestures, not keystrokes), but the walker now pays for a lookup only the list planner uses; a lazy getter or a second callback shape would avoid it.
